title: 1 Kings 10
paragraphs: ¹ The queen of Sheba heard reports of Solomon's fame, and came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions. ² She arrived with a great caravan — camels loaded with spices, vast quantities of gold, and precious stones — and when she came to Solomon, she spoke with him about everything that was on her mind. ³ Solomon answered all her questions. Nothing was too difficult for him; there was nothing he could not explain. ⁴ When the queen of Sheba saw all of Solomon's wisdom, and the palace he had built, ⁵ and the food at his table, the seating of his officials, the service of his attendants, their fine clothing, his cupbearers, and the steps by which he went up to the LORD's house — she was overwhelmed and left breathless.

⁶ She said to the king, "Everything I heard in my own country about your achievements and your wisdom is true. ⁷ I didn't believe it until I came and saw it with my own eyes — and even then, the half was not told me. Your wisdom and prosperity far exceed anything I heard. ⁸ How blessed are your people! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you always and hear your wisdom! ⁹ Praise be to the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and placed you on the throne of Israel. Because of the LORD's eternal love for Israel, he has made you king to maintain justice and righteousness." ¹⁰ Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, along with a huge quantity of spices and precious stones. Never again did such an abundance of spices arrive as what the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

¹¹ Hiram's fleet, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought great cargoes of almug wood and precious stones. ¹² The king used the almug wood to make supports for the LORD's house and for the royal palace, and to make harps and lyres for the musicians. No almug wood like it has ever been seen since. ¹³ King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she asked for, besides what he gave her from his royal generosity. Then she and her attendants returned to her own country. ¹⁴ The weight of gold that Solomon received each year was six hundred and sixty-six talents, ¹⁵ not counting what came from the revenues of merchants and traders, from all the kings of Arabia, and from the governors of the land.

¹⁶ King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold — six hundred shekels of gold for each one. ¹⁷ He also made three hundred smaller shields of hammered gold, each containing three minas of gold, and he put them all in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon. ¹⁸ The king also made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with the finest gold. ¹⁹ The throne had six steps, and its back had a rounded top. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each armrest. ²⁰ And twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at each end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any other kingdom.

²¹ All of King Solomon's drinking goblets were gold, and all the furnishings of the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Nothing was made of silver — silver was considered worthless in Solomon's day. ²² The king had a fleet of trading ships at sea together with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years it came in, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks. ²³ King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom. ²⁴ The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart. ²⁵ Year after year, every visitor brought a gift — objects of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.

²⁶ Solomon accumulated chariots and horses. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and kept with him in Jerusalem. ²⁷ The king made silver as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as common as the sycamore trees in the foothills. ²⁸ Solomon also imported horses from Egypt and from Kue — the royal merchants purchased them from Kue at the prevailing price. ²⁹ A chariot from Egypt cost six hundred shekels of silver and a horse a hundred and fifty. They exported them at these prices to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
